Sorry to bother you so late; I will head off first.

meanings.note: Numeral yī; shifts tone to yí before 4th tone and yì before 1st/2nd/3rd.

examples.trans: Give me a cup of tea.

meanings.note: Negator bù; rises to bú before a 4th-tone syllable.

examples.trans: This does not count as a big problem.
No need to wait for me.

meanings.note: Adverb yě placed strictly before the verb.

examples.trans: This is also a good thing.
I do not have that habit.

meanings.note: Particle le marking completion after a verb or a new situation at the end of a sentence.
Classifier jiàn for events, matters, and upper garments.

examples.trans: Very good, but I am curious.

meanings.note: Adverb xiān placed before the action verb.
Imperative negator bié ('don't'), often paired with final 了.

examples.trans: Twelve Singers is a hit show.

meanings.note: Sentence-final particle ma turning a statement into a yes-no question.
Final particle ba softening suggestions ('let's') or seeking confirmation ('right?').
Colloquial sentence-final particle ya softening a question.

examples.trans: Why did you ask me out here?
What will she do in which department?
I want to tell you one thing.

I want a cup of hot coffee.

meanings.note: Casual farewell huítóu jiàn ('catch you later').

examples.trans: I am going to a meeting first, see you later!

meanings.note: Third-person female pronoun tā, pronounced identically to 他.

meanings.note: Adverb jiù marking immediacy, 'just/merely', or a direct consequence.
